title: R1/R2/R3 residence districts (first ZR 23-21 table row) - maximum residential floor area ratio (standard zoning lots)
description: DRAFT extraction (needs_review) of the maximum residential floor area ratio for standard zoning lots in the FIRST row of the ZR 23-21 table: R1-2A, R1-1, R1-2, R2A, R2, R3A, R3X, R3-1 and R3-2 (standard-zoning-lot FAR 0.75; qualifying-residential-sites FAR 1.00). NOT a Verified determination - a candidate representation awaiting raw-HTML source verification and G6 qualified-human legal approval. The engine computes the standard-zoning-lot FAR and the resulting maximum residential floor area from the lot area; the higher qualifying-residential-sites FAR is surfaced as a conditional alternative (never silently applied), and the ZR 23-21 footnote-1 single-dwelling-unit equivalent-FAR cap of 0.60 - which the byte-verified recapture (commit 17e8eb78) proved is attached to THIS first table row's standard value only - is surfaced as a documented limitation. effective_from is the section's Last Amended date (2024-12-05): evaluating as_of an earlier date yields a visible not-effective outcome rather than applying today's values to a period this draft does not represent.

citations.quote: MAXIMUM FLOOR AREA RATIO FOR R1-R5 DISTRICTS. R1-2A, R1-1, R1-2, R2A, R2, R3A, R3X, R3-1, R3-2 | Standard zoning lots 0.75(footnote 1) | Qualifying residential sites 1.00

inputs.name: zoning_district
inputs.description: The residence district governing the lot (or the portion under evaluation). District SCOPE is enforced by applicability (in_set the first ZR 23-21 table row), NOT by an input domain enum: a district outside this row is a visible not_applicable, never an invalid input. An uncertain M2-T013 geometric assignment is passed via spatial_context and downgrades coverage.

inputs.name: lot_area_sq_ft
inputs.description: Zoning-lot area in square feet; must be strictly positive. A zero/negative/non-finite value is rejected fail-closed (professional_review_required, no computed value).

inputs.name: site_class
inputs.description: Whether the lot is a standard zoning lot or a 'qualifying residential site'. When absent, the qualifying-site alternative is surfaced as conditional (not decided).

outputs.name: max_residential_far
outputs.description: Maximum residential floor area ratio for a standard zoning lot in the district (ZR 23-21 first-row standard value 0.75).

outputs.name: max_residential_floor_area_sq_ft
outputs.description: Maximum residential floor area = lot area x FAR.

parameters.name: standard_far_by_district
parameters.note: Standard-zoning-lot maximum residential FAR (0.75) for every district in the first ZR 23-21 table row. Candidate values pending raw-HTML verification and G6 approval.

parameters.name: qualifying_far_by_district
parameters.note: Qualifying-residential-sites maximum residential FAR (1.00) for the first ZR 23-21 table row. SURFACED as the conditional alternative (see the qualifying_residential_site exception), never applied by this rule: whether a lot is a qualifying residential site is a separate legal determination. Provenance-linked here so the value is byte-checkable against the snapshot; it is deliberately not consumed by a computation step so the standard value is the only computed result.

steps.note: Select the standard-zoning-lot maximum residential FAR for the district (ZR 23-21 first row = 0.75).
Maximum residential floor area = lot area (sq ft) x FAR.

exceptions.description: A higher maximum residential floor area ratio (the qualifying-residential-sites value 1.00 per ZR 23-21) applies to zoning lots that are 'qualifying residential sites'. Whether a specific lot qualifies is a separate legal determination and is not decided by this rule; when the site class is unknown or qualifying, the result is conditional and the higher FAR may apply.
exceptions.note: Surfaced, never collapsed: the standard-lot FAR is reported with an explicit conditional flag that a qualifying-site FAR (1.00) may govern.

exceptions.description: For standard zoning lots with a lot area of 4,000 square feet or more, the residential floor area associated with any single dwelling unit may not exceed an equivalent floor area ratio of 0.60 (ZR 23-21 footnote 1). The byte-verified recapture (commit 17e8eb78) proved footnote 1 is attached to this first table row's standard value ONLY; it does NOT apply to R2X, R4, R5 or their variants. Applying this cap requires per-dwelling-unit inputs this rule does not model.

special_district_interactions.description: Special Purpose Districts (ZR Articles VIII-XIV) and other mapped overlays may modify residence-district floor area. When a mapped special district applies, its provisions govern and must be evaluated by the corresponding special rule; this general rule does not apply the modification.

uncertainty_policy.note: An uncertain, split, sliver, or invalid M2-T013 geometric district assignment is never collapsed into a single definitive district: coverage is downgraded to professional_review_required (or data_conflict) and the geometric uncertainty is recorded in the trace.

limitations: Draft extraction pending raw-HTML source verification and G6 qualified-human legal approval; not a Verified determination.

Only the standard-zoning-lot residential FAR is computed; the qualifying-residential-site FAR (1.00) and the per-single-dwelling-unit 0.60 equivalent-FAR cap are surfaced (conditional / documented limitation), not computed.
Special Purpose District and other overlay modifications are not applied.
